sources.entry: mr-mig/every-programmer-should-know: a collection of (mostly) technical things every software developer should know

summary.one_liner: A curated, opinionated list of links to articles, books, videos, and practice sites covering technical and career topics every software developer should know.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style link list rather than a software project. It is organized into topical sections such as Algorithms, Data Structures, Numbers, Strings, Latency, Time, Memory, Distributed Systems, Security, Architecture, Code Design, Practices, Career, Remote Work, Soft Skills, and Platform Engineering. Each entry is a resource (book, article, video, or site) with a short description for some items. The author states the list is highly opinionated, not backed by science, and unordered. Coverage also includes coding practice sites, licenses, and a few tool and service links such as Public APIs and Simpleicons.
use_cases: find learning resources on computer science fundamentals
look up books and talks for software engineering practice
prepare for technical interviews and career moves
find reading on security, distributed systems, or time/Unicode pitfalls
notable: Broad topical sections spanning CS theory, practice, career, and soft skills in one list
Includes a short section on Platform Engineering with links to Microsoft Learn, Atlassian, Spotify, and Red Hat articles
Covers niche pitfall references such as falsehoods programmers believe and Unicode/timezone problems
Labels resources by type (book, video, article) in the list entries
caveats: Explicitly highly opinionated and not backed by science, per the README
Entries are bare links with little description, so quality and currency vary
Contains a README banner promoting an external quiz, which is not part of the list content
